predecessors.name: Achaemenid Empire
predecessors.text: 'His domain encompassed Bactria, the main center', and Sogdia, after Darius III was seized in mid-330 BC

successors.name: Kingdom of Macedon
successors.text: Bactria and Sogdia, which Alexander took in the campaign that ended with Bessus's capture

ledger.x: 330: Bessus is proclaimed Artaxerxes V at Bactra.
330: the eastern Achaemenid satrapies follow Bessus.
329: Alexander crosses the Hindu Kush and Bessus's troops disperse.
329: Bessus is arrested by his Sogdian officers, Spitamenes among them, and handed over; 'He was finally sent to Ecbatana, where the Macedonians had him executed' (infobox 329, summer).
329: Bactria and Sogdia pass to Alexander.
329: the last claimant of the Achaemenid throne dies.

wars.name: Alexander's pursuit of Bessus
wars.outcome: Bessus fled across the Oxus into Sogdia; his Sogdian officers, including Spitamenes, arrested him and the Macedonians executed him at Ecbatana (329).

certainty.note: No page gives boundaries; Bactria and Sogdia are the regions.
